title: APAC build-out spreads as capital and constraints collide
lede: The week of August 10-16 underscored how Asia-Pacific data center development is simultaneously broadening geographically and straining against physical limits. In Japan, new hub proposals in Ishikari and a roughly $13 billion AI campus in Akita signaled a decisive push beyond the Tokyo-Osaka corridor, aided by cool climates, land, and offshore wind. South Korea's AI build-out accelerated on multiple fronts — telecom operators passed 1 trillion won in AI data center sales, construction firms doubled down, and the government weighed an underwater facility — even as Seoul residents resisted new sites and policymakers called for tighter regulation. Capital kept flowing: STT GDC secured $1.37 billion in green financing for Johor, Malaysian landowners sold Cyberjaya parcels to data center buyers, a Singapore operator targeted a $5 billion US IPO, and Macquarie circled Stack's $25 billion APAC portfolio. Beneath the momentum, JLL's record 25GW global absorption figures came with warnings about power, water, and mineral supply constraints shaping where capacity can realistically land.

themes.heading: Japan's build-out moves beyond Tokyo and Osaka
themes.narrative: Japanese data center development is spreading into regional areas as power and land constraints bite in the traditional hubs. An NTT-backed consortium targeted Ishikari in Hokkaido as a new hub leveraging cool climate and available power, while Akita is set to host the country's largest AI data center at an estimated 2 trillion yen (about $13 billion), backed by offshore wind. The Akita project's cost estimate was revised upward from earlier projections during the week.
themes.heading_zh: 日本的数据中心建设热潮扩展至东京和大阪之外
themes.narrative_zh: 随着电力和土地约束在传统枢纽地区日益收紧，日本的数据中心开发正在向地方区域扩散。由NTT支持的财团将北海道的石狩（Ishikari）定位为新的枢纽，利用当地凉爽的气候和可用的电力资源；与此同时，秋田将建设日本最大的AI数据中心，预计投资2万亿日元（约130亿美元），并由海上风电提供支撑。秋田项目的成本估算在本周较此前的预测有所上调。

themes.heading: Korea's AI data center machine picks up speed
themes.narrative: South Korea's AI infrastructure push gathered momentum across telecom and construction sectors. The country's three major telecom operators collectively surpassed 1 trillion won in AI data center-related sales, underlining their growing role as infrastructure builders. Hanwha Construction joined a government-backed efficiency project, while Korean builders more broadly repositioned data centers as a core growth business.
themes.heading_zh: 韩国的AI数据中心引擎加速运转
themes.narrative_zh: 韩国的AI基础设施建设在电信和建筑行业持续升温。韩国三大电信运营商的AI数据中心相关销售额合计突破1万亿韩元，凸显其作为基础设施建设者日益重要的角色。韩华建设（Hanwha Construction）加入了一个政府支持的能效项目，而韩国建筑企业也在更广泛的层面将数据中心重新定位为核心增长业务。

themes.heading: Siting backlash forces Korea to look offshore
themes.narrative: Rapid construction is triggering resistance in South Korea, with policymakers and communities demanding tighter regulation over power consumption, grid strain, and siting disputes around Seoul. Residents are openly opposing facilities near their neighborhoods, complicating new development. The pressure has pushed authorities to explore an underwater data center concept that would sidestep land scarcity while using seawater for cooling.
themes.heading_zh: 选址遭反对迫使韩国转向海上
themes.narrative_zh: 快速的建设正在韩国引发阻力，政策制定者和社区要求加强监管，涉及电力消耗、电网压力以及首尔周边的选址争议。居民公开反对在其社区附近建设设施，使新项目的开发更加复杂。这一压力促使有关部门探索水下数据中心概念，以绕过土地稀缺问题，同时利用海水进行冷却。

themes.heading: Malaysian land rush extends into new states
themes.narrative: Malaysia's data center land market stayed active, with a major property developer selling a 36-acre Cyberjaya parcel and MRCB disposing of seven Cyberjaya sites to a Singapore-backed buyer for US$102 million. The wave is spreading geographically too, as DPS Resources began exploring developments in Melaka. The deals confirm Malaysia's established tech corridor as the region's busiest land market.
themes.heading_zh: 马来西亚圈地热潮蔓延至更多州属
themes.narrative_zh: 马来西亚的数据中心土地市场保持活跃，一家大型房地产开发商出售了位于赛城（Cyberjaya）的36英亩地块，MRCB也以1.02亿美元的价格将赛城的七处地块出售给一家由新加坡支持的买家。这波热潮也在地理上扩展，DPS Resources开始探索在马六甲的开发项目。这些交易确认马来西亚成熟的科技走廊是该地区最活跃的土地市场。

themes.heading: Capital markets chase APAC data center assets
themes.narrative: Financing activity was intense across the region. STT GDC secured a US$1.37 billion green facility for its flagship Johor campus, while Centuria and ResetData fast-tracked a 250MW Australian AI pipeline with A$165 million in GPU financing, a A$300 million equity raise, a 7MW capacity deal with CDC, and a Macquarie bridge facility. Macquarie is also reportedly eyeing Stack Infrastructure's APAC portfolio, valued at more than $25 billion.
themes.heading_zh: 资本市场追逐亚太地区数据中心资产
themes.narrative_zh: 整个地区的融资活动十分活跃。STT GDC为其旗舰级柔佛园区获得了一笔13.7亿美元的绿色融资；与此同时，Centuria和ResetData加速推进250MW的澳大利亚AI项目管线，包括1.65亿澳元的GPU融资、3亿澳元的股权融资、与CDC达成的7MW容量协议，以及麦格理（Macquarie）的过桥融资。据报道，麦格理还在关注Stack Infrastructure的亚太资产组合，估值超过250亿美元。

themes.heading: Record demand runs into physical supply limits
themes.narrative: JLL reported record global absorption of 25GW in the first half of 2026, roughly doubling year-over-year on AI and cloud demand. But the week's commentary focused on the constraints: the OCP APAC Summit centered on managing AI facilities amid growing power limitations, critical mineral supply chains for copper, lithium and rare earths are straining, and fiber capacity is becoming a bottleneck as AI deployments spread.
themes.heading_zh: 创纪录的需求遭遇实体供应瓶颈
themes.narrative_zh: JLL报告称，2026年上半年全球数据中心净吸纳量达到创纪录的25GW，受AI和云需求推动，同比大约翻了一番。但本周的评论聚焦于各种约束：OCP亚太峰会的核心议题是在电力限制日益加剧的背景下管理AI设施；铜、锂和稀土等关键矿产的供应链正在承压；随着AI部署的扩展，光纤容量也正在成为瓶颈。

project_milestones.name: ResetData deployment at CDC Data Centres

title_zh: 资本涌入与制约因素交织，亚太地区数据中心建设加速铺开
lede_zh: 8月10日至16日这一周凸显了亚太地区data center的发展正同时在地理上向外扩张，并日益受到物理条件的制约。在日本，石狩的新枢纽提案以及秋田一处约130亿美元的AI园区，标志着行业向东京—大阪走廊以外地区迈出了决定性的一步，凉爽的气候、充足的土地和海上风电为此提供了助力。韩国的AI建设在多条战线上加速推进——电信运营商的AI data center销售额突破1万亿韩元，建筑企业加大投入，政府还在考虑建设水下设施——与此同时，首尔居民抵制新址建设，政策制定者呼吁加强监管。资本持续涌入：STT GDC为柔佛项目获得13.7亿美元绿色融资，马来西亚的土地所有者将赛城（Cyberjaya）的地块出售给data center买家
